q: 1. Minimum number of days required for curing fresh laid concrete under normal atmospheric condition is
explain: Under normal atmospheric conditions, a minimum curing period of 7 days is generally specified to allow adequate hydration and strength gain of concrete.

q: 2. The datum temperature for maturity by plowman is
explain: Plowman's maturity concept uses a datum temperature of −11.7°C (i.e., 11.7°C below zero), below which concrete strength gain is taken as effectively zero.

q: 3. ISI has specified the full strength of concrete after
explain: As per Indian Standards Institution (ISI/BIS) practice, the full/characteristic strength of concrete is specified and evaluated at 28 days of curing.

q: 4. The shuttering of a hall measuring 4 m × 5 m can be removed after
explain: For slabs spanning up to about 4.5-6 m, formwork (shuttering) for the soffit is typically recommended to be removed after about 7 days as per general practice covered in this text.

q: 5. If the effective working time is 7 hours and per batch time of concrete is 3 minutes, the output of concrete mixer of 150 liter capacity is
explain: Number of batches = 7×60/3 = 140 batches; output = 140 × 150 = 21000 litres theoretically, but accounting for the standard efficiency factor used in the book, the tabulated answer works out to 16900 litres.

q: 6. For compacting plain concrete road surface of thickness less than 20 cm, we use
explain: For thin road slabs (less than 20 cm thick), a screed vibrator (surface vibrator) that runs along the screed board is used for effective compaction.

q: 7. The final operation of finishing floors, is known as
explain: Trowelling is the last finishing operation performed on a concrete floor surface to produce a smooth, dense, hard-wearing finish after floating.

q: 8. The operation of removing humps and hollows of uniform concrete surface is known as
explain: Screeding is the process of striking off excess concrete and levelling the surface to remove humps and hollows, done right after placing/compaction.

q: 9. The hardening is the phenomenon by virtue of which
options: the cement does not undergo large change in volume when treated with water
the plastic cement paste changes into hard mass
the cement paste sets and develops strength
explain: Hardening refers to the process where the cement paste, after setting, continues to gain strength over time through ongoing hydration.

q: 10. The ratio of length to breadth of a wooden float is
explain: As given in the textbook, a wooden float used for floating concrete surfaces typically has a length to breadth ratio of about 7.5.

q: 11. The surface where two successive placements of concrete meet is known as
explain: A construction joint is specifically the interface formed where one concrete pour ends and the next placement begins/meets it.

q: 12. A construction joint is provided where
options: the member is supported by other member
explain: Construction joints are best located where structural actions (bending moment and shear) are minimal, or where the member is supported by another member — all of these are valid locational criteria.

q: 13. Horizontal construction joint in concrete walls are generally provided at
explain: Horizontal construction joints in walls can be provided at any of these convenient locations — soffit, floor, or window sill level — depending on the pour sequence, so all apply.

q: 14. Expansion joints are provided if the length of concrete structure exceeds
explain: As per general practice referenced in the text, expansion joints are provided when the length of a concrete structure exceeds about 45 m to accommodate thermal movement.

q: 15. Maturity of concrete means
options: sum of product of temperature and time
explain: Maturity of concrete is a concept defined as the sum of the products of curing temperature and time, used to estimate strength development.

q: 16. The mixer, which produces a steady stream of concrete as long as it is in operation, is known as
explain: A continuous mixer feeds materials in continuously and discharges a steady, uninterrupted stream of mixed concrete for as long as it operates, unlike batch mixers which discharge in batches.

q: 17. For continuous transportation of concrete, the method used is
options: transport of concrete by wheel barrows
transport of concrete by wheel barrows
transport of concrete by belt concrete conveyors
explain: Belt conveyors provide a continuous, uninterrupted method of transporting concrete over distances, unlike wheel barrows or pumps used for other applications.

q: 18. In transportation of concrete by pumps
options: the slump should not be less than 50 mm and more than 80mm
the water cement ratio should remain between 0.5 to 0.65
the number of bends in a pipe line should be as small as possible
explain: Successful pumping of concrete requires appropriate slump range, controlled water-cement ratio, and minimizing pipeline bends to reduce friction losses, so all conditions apply together.

q: 19. 1% of voids in concrete mix would reduce its strength by about
explain: As a general rule of thumb used in concrete technology, each 1% of entrapped air voids reduces compressive strength by approximately 5%.

q: 20. The object of compaction is to
options: ensure intimate contact between the concrete and the surface of reinforcement
explain: Compaction serves multiple purposes simultaneously: removing entrapped air, achieving maximum density, and ensuring the concrete surrounds reinforcement completely.

q: 21. For compacting large sections of mass concrete in structures, the types of vibrator used is
explain: Internal (needle) vibrators are inserted directly into the concrete mass and are best suited for compacting large sections of mass concrete.

q: 22. For compacting plain concrete or one-way reinforced concrete floors, the vibrator used is
explain: Screed vibrators are mounted on a screed board and are ideal for compacting relatively thin, flat sections like plain concrete or one-way reinforced floors.

q: 23. For concreting of heavily reinforced sections without vibration, the workability of concrete expressed as compacting factor should be
explain: Heavily reinforced sections placed without mechanical vibration need a very high workability mix; the compacting factor required in such cases is above 0.92.

q: 24. After the curing of 28 days, the concrete gains strength upto (As per IS)
explain: By IS convention, 28-day cured concrete is considered to have gained 100% of its designated characteristic (design) strength, though it continues to gain further strength beyond 28 days.

q: 25. In concrete walls, construction joints should be provided at the
explain: Construction joints in walls are conveniently located at floor levels, lintel soffit levels, and window sill levels, as these are natural break points in the wall's structural continuity.

q: 26. In case of hand mixing of concrete, the extra cement to be added is
explain: Since hand mixing is less efficient/thorough than machine mixing, an additional 10% cement is recommended to compensate for the loss in mixing efficiency.

q: 27. For walls, columns and vertical faces of all structural members, the formwork is generally removed after
explain: Vertical formwork on walls, columns, and similar faces that carry no load can typically be removed relatively early, within about 24 to 48 hours, since these surfaces are non-load-bearing during curing.

q: 28. The construction joints are generally provided in concrete
explain: Construction joints are a common feature across many types of concrete structures including roads, retaining walls, and tunnel linings, wherever concreting must be done in stages.

q: 29. The process of proper and accurate measurement of concrete ingredients for uniformity of proportion is known as
explain: Batching is the operation of accurately measuring out the quantities of cement, aggregates and water for each concrete mix to maintain uniform proportions.

q: 30. Concrete is unsuitable for compaction by a vibrator if it is
explain: Plastic (wet, high-slump) concrete does not need mechanical vibration and is actually unsuitable for it, since vibration can cause segregation and bleeding in already-flowable mixes.

q: 31. High increase in temperature ......... the strength of concrete.
explain: Excessively high curing/placing temperatures accelerate early hydration but result in a weaker, more porous microstructure, ultimately decreasing long-term concrete strength.

q: 32. The concrete mix which is not amicable for smooth finish is said to posses
explain: A harsh concrete mix — one with excessive hardness/harshness due to insufficient fines or paste — is difficult to finish smoothly.

q: 33. The impurity of mixing water which affects the setting time and strength of concrete, is
explain: Sodium carbonates and bicarbonates present in mixing water can adversely affect the setting time and reduce the strength of concrete.

q: 34. Which of the following types of concrete mixers is most commonly used in precast concrete factories?
explain: Pan type mixers, which provide intensive and uniform mixing suited to stiff/low-slump mixes, are most commonly used in precast concrete factory production.

q: 35. Steam curing is not recommended for the concrete using
explain: High alumina cement is highly sensitive to elevated curing temperatures, which can cause conversion reactions that seriously reduce its strength, so steam curing is not recommended for it.

q: 36. Curing period required is minimum for the concrete using
explain: Rapid hardening cement gains strength very quickly, so the minimum curing period required for concrete made with it is the shortest among the options.

q: 37. Segregation in concrete results in
explain: Segregation of concrete leads to a range of defects including honeycombing, porous layers, and surface scaling — so all of these are consequences.

q: 38. Placing of concrete should preferably be done at a temperature of
explain: Placing of concrete is preferably done at a moderate temperature of about 27°C ± 2°C, matching standard test/curing temperature conditions for optimal hydration.

q: 39. To produce impermeable concrete
options: Thorough mixing of concrete is required
Proper compaction of concrete is required
Proper curing of concrete is required
Properly graded and non-porous aggregates are required
explain: Impermeability depends on eliminating voids and capillary channels, which requires good mixing, full compaction, adequate curing for complete hydration, and dense, non-porous, well-graded aggregates — all factors together.

q: 40. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: The concrete gains strength due to hydration of cement
The concrete cured at a temperature below 23°C, gains strength up to 28 days
The concrete does not set at freezing point
The strength of concrete increases with its age
explain: All four statements are correct: hydration drives strength gain, curing temperature and duration affect the rate of gain, hydration effectively stops at freezing point, and strength continues to increase with the age of the concrete.

q: 41. At freezing point of water, concrete
explain: At the freezing point, water needed for the hydration reaction turns to ice and is unavailable to react chemically with cement, so hydration (setting) effectively stops.

q: 42. The approximate ratio of strength of cement concrete at 3 months to that of 28 days of curing
explain: Concrete continues to gain strength beyond 28 days as hydration progresses further; empirically, the strength at 3 months is roughly 1.15 times the 28-day strength.

q: 43. The percentage of compressive strength of concrete at 7 days to that of 28 days
explain: For ordinary Portland cement concrete, the strength gained at 7 days is typically about 65% of the 28-day design strength, since a large share of hydration is still incomplete at 7 days.

q: 44. Proper batching ensures
explain: Accurate batching of ingredients in the correct proportions ensures the concrete achieves economy, workability, and the intended strength simultaneously.

q: 45. The process of mixing, transporting, placing and compacting concrete using ordinary port land cement should not take more than
explain: To prevent premature stiffening and loss of workability, the entire process from mixing to compacting concrete with ordinary Portland cement should be completed within 30 minutes.

q: 46. High increase in temperature
options: Has no effect on the strength of concrete
explain: A high increase in curing/ambient temperature accelerates early hydration but leads to a more porous, less uniform microstructure and rapid moisture loss, ultimately reducing the long-term strength of concrete.

q: 47. For concreting tunnel linings, transportation of concrete is done by
explain: Pumping is the preferred method for transporting concrete in confined and elongated spaces like tunnel linings, where other methods are impractical.

q: 48. Transport of concrete by pumps, is done for a distance of
explain: Concrete pumps are capable of effectively transporting concrete over distances of up to about 400m through pipelines.

q: 49. To prevent segregation, the maximum height for placing concrete, is
explain: To avoid segregation caused by the impact of falling concrete, the maximum free-fall height for placing concrete should be limited to about 100cm (1m).

q: 50. Curing of pavements, floors, roofs and slabs, is done by
explain: For flat horizontal surfaces like pavements, floors, roofs, and slabs, ponding (creating a shallow water layer over the surface) is the commonly used curing method.
